name: Multi-Instance Detection Pipeline
description: Detect candidates in input data, classify each candidate independently, then aggregate instance-level predictions to produce a bag-level output. The DSB2017 lung cancer solution is the canonical example: detect nodules in CT, classify each nodule, aggregate via noisy-OR. Generalizes to any multi-instance learning problem.
applicable_when: Input contains multiple instances (objects, regions, candidates) per sample
Final prediction aggregates instance-level scores to a sample-level prediction
relationship_to_tabular: This is an expansion of the tabular pipeline where model_training is replaced by a detect → classify → aggregate sub-CDG. The feature_engineering and output nodes remain the same.

nodes.name: preprocess
nodes.description: Domain-specific preprocessing. For medical imaging: segmentation, resampling, normalization. For object detection: resize, augment.

nodes.name: detect_candidates
nodes.description: Detect candidate instances in the preprocessed input. Produces a list of candidate locations/proposals with confidence scores. For 3D medical imaging, this is a 3D anchor-based detector with NMS.

nodes.name: extract_instance_features
nodes.description: For each detected candidate, extract a feature representation. This may be a crop from a feature map, a pooled vector, or hand-crafted features.

nodes.name: classify_instances
nodes.description: Score each candidate instance independently. Produces per-instance probabilities.

nodes.name: aggregate_to_sample
nodes.description: Aggregate instance-level predictions to a sample-level prediction. The choice of aggregation is critical: max, mean, and noisy-OR have very different behavior. Noisy-OR with a learned baseline (from DSB2017) is the most principled for detection problems because it handles the 'detector missed everything' case.
